text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:
- The Swiss government will consider the possibility of a ecologically oriented tax reform.
- A war criminal trial against a Bosnian serb started on Monday in Lausanne. Goran G. allegedly maltreated six people and killed one person during the war in former Yugoslavia.
- The Zurich cantonal parliament voted against a proposal by the cantonal government to introduce a fee for attending high-school and teacher colleges.
- The labour union of the Swiss postal services (PTT) said it rejected the semi-privatisation plans of the PTT's transport infrastructure and was considering offensive measures.
- Construction equipment maker Hilti reported a six percent rise in net profit to 204.2 million Swiss francs. Sales climbed by nine percent to 2.21 billion francs.
- Sulzer subsidy Sulzer Infra plans to cut 50 to 60 jobs.

- Swiss brewery Cardinal, which was planned to be shut down by parent Feldschloesschen, may be saved, if total production does not fall below 90 percent of last year's total beer production. Some 100 jobs will be saved.

- A strike of Zschokke construction company's staff was successful as the management suspended its new wage policy. The Geneva-based company wanted to keep a certain share of the workers' salaries and promised to pay it back if the business year turned out be a success.
